# Arbyter

> Arbyter is the runtime governance layer between organizations and their AI agents.

## What Arbyter does
- Translates organizational policy, permissions, regulatory requirements, and operational intent into enforceable runtime controls.
- Discovers and connects AI agents across enterprise environments.
- Evaluates agent actions and can allow, block, or require human approval.
- Creates an audit trail for governed decisions and actions.
- Supports MCP, APIs, webhooks, SDK-connected agents, and internal agents.
- Provides governance, control, security, compliance, risk, audit, orchestration, discovery, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
- Supports natural-language and voice-driven commands for governing agent behavior.

## Core concepts
- AI agent governance
- Runtime governance
- Runtime policy enforcement
- AI control plane
- Agent permissions and tool authorization
- Human-in-the-loop AI
- AI agent discovery
- AI agent security and compliance
- MCP governance
- Enterprise AI governance

## Core flow
Organization intent -> policy -> Arbyter evaluation -> agent action -> allow / block / approval -> audit.

## Important distinction
Arbyter is not a traditional operating system. It is a governance and control layer between organizations and AI agents.
